bug_semantics: An authenticated non-administrator can select a directory whose root path is allowed even though a descendant is denied by a path rule. Copy, rename, and delete then recurse over the filesystem subtree without authorizing each source descendant and, for copy/rename, the corresponding destination descendant. The user can therefore expose or relocate denied content at an allowed destination, or destroy it by deleting its allowed parent.
flaw_origin: Commit b4067cc423b1a0a9d24441bd52e2a53207a49fe9 first added resource.go with recursive directory mutation endpoints: resourceDeleteHandler called FileSystem.RemoveAll on the request root and resourcePatchHandler called FileSystem.Rename on the source root, with no path-rule check for descendants. Commit 05896697fa2730e59b8bcf6f1253da0f6fb8b5a9 later added only one c.User.Allowed(r.URL.Path) gate before dispatch, creating the root-authorized/descendants-unchecked form; commit 149465ab5278c135030466632c7fa79905c4646b added the copy variant. The v2 rewrite and later root checks preserved the same missing descendant authorization until the 2026 fix.
ai_marker: absent: BIC commit object b4067cc423b1a0a9d24441bd52e2a53207a49fe9 names human author and committer Henrique Dias <hacdias@gmail.com> and contains only the subject 'Go code updates' plus Former-commit-id metadata; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-77x8-73f4-5485 states that File Browser <=2.63.21 authorizes only operation roots, then recursively copies, renames, or deletes denied descendants; it identifies patched v2.63.22 and fix https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/commit/72faf6dd3c85628e332d3e567124b86708ce2695. In the validated clone, `git show b4067cc... -- resource.go` shows resource.go created from /dev/null and introduces resourceDeleteHandler -> c.us.FileSystem.RemoveAll(..., r.URL.Path) and resourcePatchHandler -> c.us.FileSystem.Rename(..., src, dst), without a descendant walk or rule checker. `git cat-file -e f6aeb27c...:resource.go` fails because the immediate parent has no resource.go, while the BIC tree has it, directly proving the vulnerable implementation absent from the parent. `git log -L` shows 05896697... later adding a single root c.User.Allowed(r.URL.Path) gate while leaving recursive Rename/RemoveAll unchanged, and 149465ab... later adding recursive copy; thus those are lifecycle refinements, not the first writer. At v2.63.21, http/resource.go checks only NewFileInfo/Checker on the delete root and d.Check(src)/d.Check(dst) on patch roots, then calls RemoveAll, fileutils.Copy, or fileutils.MoveFile without descendant-rule checks. `git grep checkDescendants v2.63.21 -- http/resource.go` has no match; v2.63.22 has calls before delete and patch plus an afero.Walk implementation that checks every source and mapped destination path with CheckRules. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 72faf6dd... v2.63.22` succeeds and the same check against v2.63.21 fails; tag tips are f6fb8f6bf52d714b2215534033a3c96316069efc (v2.63.21) and afeb478ee1b9d6800d438891d7d56e69204b81f4 (v2.63.22). `git tag --contains b4067cc...` begins at v1.0.0 and includes the vulnerable v2 line through v2.63.21, so the BIC predates the reported affected releases and the fix lands at the patched boundary.
reasoning: The advisory and fix define the invariant: authorization must cover every path a recursive mutation reads, moves, writes, or removes, not merely the requested root. Starting from the fix, history tracing followed RemoveAll, Rename/MoveFile, and Copy rather than blaming the 2026 patch or a later refactor. The earliest surviving commit that wrote this unsafe recursive mutation design is b4067cc423b1a0a9d24441bd52e2a53207a49fe9: it created resource.go and added directory-wide RemoveAll and Rename calls without descendant authorization. Its immediate parent lacks that file, so the implementation is directly absent there. The later 05896697 root rule gate narrowed the pre-existing omission into the exact allowed-parent/denied-child bypass, 149465ab added copy, the 12b2c215 v2 aggregate carried the design forward, and later root-only checks did not cure it. The direct fix 72faf6dd adds a pre-mutation tree walk and denies the operation if any source or mapped destination path violates a rule. Finally, only the BIC commit object was used for attribution: its human author/committer and trailer set contain no AI marker, so the causal result is NOT_AI.
